rationale: The persona prizes mechanism-focused diagnostics that cleanly distinguish hypotheses. Option 1 uses grading failure despite policy-compliant actions — a signal specifically indicative of benchmark flaws (not task difficulty) — and then attributes each flaw to one of the three hypothesized mechanisms. Option 2's aggregate low-success signal is confounded: hard tasks also produce low success and stronger-agent failures, so it cannot cleanly separate flawed tasks from genuinely difficult ones.
